emerging_technology: Generative artificial intelligence, with large language models as the evidenced subset
intended_application: Use approved product specifications and raw product images to propose a headline, three key specifications, a caption, and image placement, plus a visual mockup for retouching in Canva for Instagram or YouTube.
organization: Hypothetical textile manufacturer marketing team inspired by Lucy Shen’s reported workflow; organizational controls and resources below are case assumptions.
business_need: Reduce the logistics of converting screenshot specifications and images into finished marketing content. Lucy targets an 80% efficiency increase; no baseline or verified benefit exists.
users_stakeholders: Lucy as content creator and final reviewer; technical product owner; marketing audience.
adoption_posture: Moderate fast follower, assumed for this test.
capabilities_constraints: Existing Canva workflow and a human reviewer are assumed. Screenshot extraction, image matching, layout generation and Canva transfer are untested complementary capabilities; RAG supplies approved reference text rather than the whole workflow.
risk_consequence_context: Wrong numbers, units, product identity or technical meaning could mislead customers. Human checks technical meaning, wording and final design before publication.
management_question: How much should broad technological significance influence whether to evaluate this bounded content workflow now?
time_horizon: Proposed four-week evaluation; longer-run significance assessed over ten years or more without predicting a date.
additional_context: Personal input is drawn from Lucy’s visible answers. She accepts a faster editable draft and wants to make final retouches. Do not present desired capabilities or efficiency as achieved. Efficiency metric must be agreed: 80% higher accepted outputs/hour equals time per output divided by 1.8, whereas 80% less time equals time multiplied by 0.2. These are different targets.
